text: An external-table reader needs SELECT on the table and REFERENCES on its database-scoped credential when present; the overview does not list a bulk-operation permission for this SELECT path. (low confidence)
keywords: Synapse serverless SQL credentials for Atlas-exported Blob files

text: Microsoft Entra passthrough uses the caller's storage identity; SQL users cannot use it. SQL users can instead use credential-backed workspace managed identity, SAS, or service principal. Storage Blob Data Reader suffices for reading; management-plane Owner alone does not grant blob data access. (high confidence)
keywords: Synapse serverless SQL credentials for Atlas-exported Blob files

text: The storage identity or SAS must permit reading and listing the exported files; SAS troubleshooting requires an unexpired token with rl permissions. For ACL-only access in hierarchical-namespace ADLS Gen2, grant Read on the file and Execute on every parent directory, plus listing permissions for queried directories. Azure evaluates role assignments before ACLs; an ACL cannot restrict access already granted by a role assignment and its conditions. (high confidence)
keywords: Synapse serverless SQL credentials for Atlas-exported Blob files

text: A reply to a reported Synapse Serverless view failure, Cannot find the CREDENTIAL 'WorkspaceIdentity', recommends GRANT REFERENCES ON DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL. This agrees with the documented credential-use grant and shows why database read membership alone may be insufficient; it is advice in the incident thread, not proof that a fix or Atlas integration was executed. (high confidence)
keywords: Synapse serverless SQL credentials for Atlas-exported Blob files

text: A SQL-login direct query with a missing or mismatched server credential can fail; directory-listing failures can instead indicate insufficient list permission on the passthrough identity, SAS or workspace identity. Diagnose credential selection separately from storage access. (high confidence)
keywords: Synapse serverless SQL credentials for Atlas-exported Blob files

text: SQL query authorization and storage authorization are separate gates. For OPENROWSET with a credential-bearing DATA_SOURCE, grant REFERENCES ON DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL::<credential> and either ADMINISTER BULK OPERATIONS or ADMINISTER DATABASE BULK OPERATIONS. A credential-free DATA_SOURCE still requires one bulk permission; SQL permission alone does not grant file access. (low confidence)
keywords: Synapse serverless SQL credentials for Atlas-exported Blob files

text: For a SQL login using OPENROWSET without DATA_SOURCE, create a URL-matching server credential and grant REFERENCES ON CREDENTIAL::<url> in master. For Blob use https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net[/<container>]. The overview permission table lists REFERENCES on the SAS credential as an alternative to the bulk privileges for this case. (high confidence)
keywords: Synapse serverless SQL credentials for Atlas-exported Blob files

text: With DATA_SOURCE, bind a database-scoped credential to EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE and set LOCATION to the exported container/prefix; the credential name need not match the URL. Managed identity uses IDENTITY='Managed Identity'; SAS uses IDENTITY='SHARED ACCESS SIGNATURE' with its token as SECRET, omitting the leading question mark. (high confidence)
keywords: Synapse serverless SQL credentials for Atlas-exported Blob files

text: Credential provisioning is privileged: server credentials require ALTER ANY CREDENTIAL in master, while database-scoped credentials require CONTROL on the user database. Database-scoped credentials and external data sources belong in a user SQL database, not master. Initialize the documented database master key; creating an external data source also requires ALTER ANY EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE and REFERENCES on its credential. (high confidence)
keywords: Synapse serverless SQL credentials for Atlas-exported Blob files

text: The access-control page lists SAS, service principal, managed identity and user identity for Blob Storage, but its firewall section allows user or managed identity and requires a workspace resource-instance exception, excluding SAS/service principal. Its cross-tenant section instead recommends service principal, disallows managed identity and lists SAS even with firewall-protected storage. Do not treat these conflicting sections as a verified cross-tenant/firewall recipe; a credential alone does not establish network access. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-01-22)
keywords: Synapse serverless SQL credentials for Atlas-exported Blob files
